title: Democrat Senate candidate falsely says Christians don’t need to believe in virgin birth
description: ( LifeSiteNews ) – A Methodist megachurch pastor nominated by Democrats for U.S. Senate in Kansas argued in a resurfaced podcast that Christians do not have to believe in the virgin birth of Jesus Christ in order to be Christian. Rev. Adam Hamilton is the pastor of the 24,000-member Church of the Resurrection in Leawood, Kansas, which Religion News described as the largest United Methodist church in America. In August, he won a crowded Democrat primary with almost 35% of the vote and the nomination to face incumbent Republican U.S. Sen. Roger Marshall in November. … The spokesperson added that Hamilton has previously written he accepts “Jesus was born of a virgin, that Christ’s death atones for our sin and ‘reconciles us to God,’ that Christ was physically raised from the dead, and that Jesus actually performed miracles when he walked on the earth”; but “rejec(t)s that the Bible is inerrant and that every word or idea was virtually dictated by God.” LifeSiteNews reported last month that Hamilton had also preached in a 2020 sermon that his listeners needed to repent for contributing to climate change, further indicating a brand of Christianity that prioritized left-wing “social justice” over biblical morality (Hamilton supports legal abortion). The Kansas Senate race has recently tightened according to multiple analysts, but Republicans hope framing Hamilton as another “woke” extremist can turn things around in a midterm election season widely seen as an uphill battle for the GOP. A similar fight is underway in Texas, where Democrats nominated Presbyterian seminarian James Talarico on the assumption his religiosity would help sell him as a mainstream candidate, only to run headfirst into Talarico’s long list of far-left positions .
